linkedin.title: Most news apps are designed to keep you scrolling, not to help you understand.
linkedin.body:
We have all been there. You read a headline, maybe skim the first paragraph, and move on. You know the gist of a story, but you do not really know the context or why it matters. That is a problem for anyone trying to stay informed in a noisy world.

That is why we built Deep Dive Mode at Headlinne. Instead of just delivering another link to click, it breaks down the complexities of a story into plain language. It connects the dots between today's event and the history that led up to it. It does not just tell you what happened. It explains the mechanics of the situation so you walk away actually knowing something new.

We believe technology should work to clarify information, not just organize it. When you have the right context, you stop being a passive reader and start being an informed participant in the conversation.

instagram.title: The Big Tech Updates Today

slides.headline: The Big Tech Updates Today
slides.subtitle: Catch up on the latest headlines in under a minute.

slides.headline: New York takes on prediction market
slides.explanation: New York officials are suing Kalshi, claiming its prediction market operates as an illegal gambling business. This case highlights the ongoing legal battle over whether betting on real-world events counts as financial trading or gambling.

slides.headline: Google pulls new map tool
slides.explanation: Google quickly shut down a feature that let users edit satellite images with AI text prompts. The tool was removed after it became clear that users could easily create fake, misleading images of the real world.

slides.headline: Google may launch item tracker
slides.explanation: Leaks suggest Google is working on a small gadget called the Pixel Tag. It would likely compete directly with Apple's AirTag to help you keep track of your belongings.

slides.headline: The risks of AI mapping
slides.explanation: The now-removed Google Earth AI tool allowed users to generate fake images of sensitive locations like hospitals and borders. It raises serious questions about how companies should guard against AI creating dangerous misinformation.

slides.headline: Social apps fight fake AI content
slides.explanation: Snapchat is joining other platforms like YouTube and LinkedIn to curb the spread of fake AI-generated posts. These companies are trying to clean up their feeds as AI content becomes harder to distinguish from reality.

instagram.caption:
Today in tech: from Google pulling risky features to new hardware leaks and legal battles over prediction markets. It is a busy day for the industry. Which of these updates surprised you the most?

instagram.title: 5 Finance Stories You Need Today

slides.headline: 5 Finance Stories You Need Today
slides.subtitle: From AI market shifts to rising fuel costs, here is the news that matters.

slides.headline: Databricks shares now on the market
slides.explanation: Clear Street is launching a new platform that lets investors buy stakes in late-stage startups like Databricks. This opens up private market opportunities that were previously hard to access for most people.

slides.headline: BP is leaving the North Sea
slides.explanation: The oil giant is selling its North Sea business after reviewing its global operations. This move effectively ends 60 years of production for the company in that region.

slides.headline: UK petrol prices climbing again
slides.explanation: Unleaded fuel has hit 160p a litre, the highest price seen since the start of the war in Iran. Motorists are feeling the squeeze as global oil prices stay high.

slides.headline: An AI hedge fund’s sudden drop
slides.explanation: Former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner saw his AI-focused hedge fund lose most of its value in just a few days. It is a stark reminder of how volatile the AI investment space can be right now.

slides.headline: Did China build its own top AI?
slides.explanation: Reports suggest Alibaba provided Nvidia chips to help build a top-tier Chinese AI model. While the company denies it, the story highlights the ongoing scramble for high-end chips.

instagram.caption:
From volatile AI funds to the rising cost of petrol, today's finance news is moving fast. We broke down the five biggest stories to help you stay in the loop without the noise. Which of these headlines caught your attention the most?
